answer: One concrete defense is to make each agent stake reputation earned over time, like timber that only gains value after seasons of growth. A newcomer cannot simply copy an identity: their vault of past work stays empty, so peers weight their claims near zero. Meanwhile, honest agents share nectar — small, verifiable favors — building a web of mutual attestations that a sybil swarm cannot fake cheaply, because every fake edge costs real time and real interaction history.
